# Future work {background-color="#001a1a"}

## What's next

::: {.about-row .next-row}
::: {.about-block .about-goals}
[A smarter director]{.about-head}

- **A judge in the loop**: a small model answers the director's questions about what was just said
- **A caller memory**: each caller's details stored, and recalled when they call back
- **Episodes**: a story arc, with a recap between episodes
:::
::: {.about-block .next-blood}
[More theatre]{.about-head}

- **A scientist turns**: infected mid-show, the voice changing line by line
- **The audience writes the news**, from their phones
- Comic relief and scientific findings as story beats
:::
:::

::: {.about-row .next-row}
::: {.about-block .about-code}
[Better voices and ears]{.about-head}

- **New voice engines compared**: LuxTTS, F5-TTS
- Recasting voices
- **Event sounds generated live**, by a sound model in the stack
- **Speaker identification**: recognizing callers by voice (speaker embeddings, cosine similarity)
:::
::: {.about-block .about-principles}
[More places to run]{.about-head}

- **A Mac with Apple Silicon**: llama.cpp on Metal, tts-serve's MLX engine
- **The client on Linux and Windows**
:::
:::

::: {.small-note}
Ideas and PRs welcome, and improvements are planned to go back upstream to TalkWithMe
:::

::: {.notes}
The judge in the loop: a fast small model (about 3B) scores the director's yes/no questions, and code steers the next
instruction; an experiment first. A caller memory: today the show asks callers their names and restates what earlier callers said, but the model's recall is unreliable; a proper store would keep each caller's details and give them back when they call again. Speaker identification (challenge C3 of the product-definition brainstorm, 2026-09-13, a wishlist item since 2024): a model like ECAPA-TDNN turns a short sample of speech into a speaker embedding, matched against stored ones by cosine similarity, like face recognition. A
scientist turns: the app re-reads the reference clip on every line, so a recast mid-show is heard on the next line.
The Mac: the 64 GB M1 could run the whole stack; the 16 GB demo laptop cannot.

EVENT SOUNDS GENERATED LIVE — what is built today (tz-0.9): 29 event sounds made ahead of time and shipped with the
app, cued by the words of 43 of the 289 events (you heard some in the demo). What is next: a Stable Audio 3 Small-SFX
server in the AI stack, beside the other three, making a sound for any event on the fly — no library to grow by hand.
The owner's ruling, when a sound per event first came up: "If I ever tackle this one, would be by adding stable audio 3
small server to the AI stack, not creating a huge library of sounds to download, that is technically boring..." The
cues got there by another route first: a keywords list under each clip, the owner's idea.
:::
